key_insight: A synthetic pipeline can produce realistic, long-form doctor–patient audio conversations and aligned SOAP-note targets, creating both a scalable training resource and a controlled evaluation suite for long-context audio summarization.
problem_solved: Addresses scarcity of long-context audio training data and the lack of controlled benchmarks for evaluating open-ended summarization of extended clinical conversations.
method: Design templated clinical scenarios and behavioral variations to generate diverse first-visit doctor–patient dialogues.
Synthesize long-form audio and transcripts (controlled noise/turns) paired with reference SOAP notes to form train/eval splits.
Use the synthetic corpus as both a training dataset for models and a controllable evaluation environment for long-context summarization tasks.
impact: Provides practitioners a reproducible way to train and benchmark models on long-context audio reasoning, accelerating development of robust clinical summarization systems while preserving privacy and experimental control.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: scenario templates → dialogue generator → audio/text synthesis → SOAP target pairs
Side-by-side example: excerpt of synthetic audio transcript vs. generated reference SOAP note
Dataset composition chart: conversation length distribution, turn counts, clinical diversity
Evaluation layout: controlled variables (noise, interruptions, prompt length) vs. model performance
paper_title: Generating Synthetic Doctor-Patient Conversations for Long-form Audio Summarization
paper_authors: Yanis Labrak, David Grünert, Séverin Baroudi, Jiyun Chun, Pawel Cyrta
